dossier_meta.catalog_title: Conjecture on optimal exponential constant for $K_t$-subdivision clique count
dossier_meta.statement_text: The maximum number of cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no $K_t$-subdivision is $3^{2t/3+o(t)}n$, i.e., the optimal exponential constant in the exponent is $\frac{2}{3}\log_2 3 \approx 1.06$.
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 1.2 establishes an upper bound of $2^{1.817t+o(t)}n$, improving on Lee and Oum. Wood's lower bound construction (which also forbids clique subdivisions) shows the constant cannot be reduced below $\frac{2}{3}\log_2 3 \approx 1.06$. The authors proved $c(t) = 3^{2t/3+o(t)}$ for $K_t$-minors in earlier work [10] and conjecture the same bound holds for $K_t$-subdivisions.
